newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle close unevenly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle close unevenly lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed unevenly lower with extremely distant months rising to new contract highs.

Live cattle closed 0.425 cent lower to 0.200 higher with February off 0.050 at 65.575 cents. Distant December and February posted new contract highs. Feeder cattle ended 0.250 cent lower to 0.300 higher with March off most at 68.450 and distant November up most to a new high.
Commercial hedge selling led to technical pressure and this generally offset commission house support prompted by weather concerns in live cattle futures, traders said.

Expectations of increased cattle supplies ahead following heavy placements onto feedlots since last fall prompted the selling interest, especially since February was near its contract high. The failure of futures to set a new high then brought on additional technical selling which offset the support from weather concerns, they said.

Cattle weights are already low and expectations that cold weather will continue for at least another week and keep weights down prompted the mixed support in futures. Death losses due to blizzard conditions and extreme cold last week added to ideas of tighter marketings into February, they said.
R.J. O'Brien generally bought February while RBH sold. Refco and Cargill Investor Services bought April and sold February, thought to be continuation of the "Goldman roll", pit sources said.

In live cattle options, there was early commission house buying of February 65 and 66 calls while scattered buying of 68 calls was cited late. There was continued hedging in April and June, pit sources added.
Feeders also retreated after showing initial strength following live cattle and another gain in the latest CME feeder cattle index.

The rally in corn futures and clipping of gains in live cattle weighed on most months of feeders. E.D.& F. Man notably sold March on the setback with Refco a late buyer. Cargill bought January while Smith Barney sold, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.29 at $67.87 per cwt.
